newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aisin wins GM order for transmission parts.
newsitem.headline: Aisin wins GM order for transmission parts.

text.p: Japan's Aisin Seiki Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had received orders for torque converters from the Allison Transmission Division (ATD) of General Motors Corp (GM) for use in commercial vehicle automatic transmissions being developed by ATD.
Aisin, owned 22.6 percent by Toyota Motor Corp, will start supplying the torque converters by the end of 1998. It will supply 40,000 in the first year, rising to 150,000 a year by 2000.

Aisin said the firms also agreed to use ATD's 1,400 service points in the United States to service Aisin automatic transmissions installed in Japanese-made light trucks imported into the United States.
Aisin said the firms had agreed to study future cooperation in production and marketing of ATD-designed commercial vehicle automatic transmissions in Japan and Asian markets.
They are also considering assembling ADT-designed automatic transmissions for heavy buses at Aisin in Japan for sale to four Japanese heavy truck and bus makers, it said.
